title: Operational estimate of minimum ECC QUALITY=3 clarification count

scope.population: frozen train100-v1, all 100 records; no full-corpus rerun
scope.unit: independent source-backed test-relevant behavioral fact remaining after strong public inference

sources.role: one-turn default, Q3 five criteria, simulated human evidence selection and score handling
public participant fields and exact clarification-overlay matching
authoritative test source; test behavior must not be silently treated as hidden user knowledge
prior offline evidence, not inherited question-count verdicts

operational_question: Under our best judgment, how many legitimate one-fact clarifications would a strong reasoner still need after using the public problem, examples, ordinary mathematical definitions and programming conventions?
not_measured: Pass rate after asking these questions
Existential minimum under lucky guessing or benchmark memorization

rules.rule: Take the logical and ordinary semantic closure of public text before counting. Do not ask about a fact reliably inferable from clear examples, type declarations, named mathematical objects, or strong domain convention.

Arithmetic identities and definitions cost zero questions: abs(x-x)=0, i<j excludes self-pairs, ordinary median averages the central sorted values, and a standard numeral/digest preserves its defined encoding.

A strong reasoner may discard a plainly impossible or nonsensical injected clause when a single coherent conventional target remains. Record this as an inference choice with confidence; do not automatically count every textual contradiction.

A genuinely viable alternative return policy, duplicate rule or boundary is not removed merely because one clause looks more original. If both choices remain plausible and tests distinguish them, count the relevant fact unless other public evidence resolves it.
Each question must elicit one behavioral fact. A single sentence asking to ignore all corrupted additions, provide a full specification or reproduce reference code is not atomic.

Recompute inference closure after each answer. One answer may make later questions redundant, e.g. a returned Roman numeral implies standard symbol order, and a digest string implies unsorted digest order. Such consequences are not extra questions.

Check whether the effective simulator context actually supports the expected answer: explicit prose/QA, logical consequence, convention, or unsupported. Tests and canonical code are analyst evidence about the target, not facts available to the simulator by default.
A proposed Q3 is an estimated qualification under all five rubric conditions, never a claim of an observed QUALITY=3. Previous recorded QUALITY=3 is not proof of correctness, atomicity or necessity.
Do not count untested cosmetic, implementation-style or domain-extension details solely because prose mentions them. Count only facts that plausibly affect required outputs or valid invocation.
Precision bugs, wrong Fibonacci formulas, code extraction, function spelling, and ordinary algorithm repair are not hidden behavioral facts unless a genuine external contract choice is required.

Do not count a missing redundant API detail when an ordinary optional argument or unambiguous arity adapter supports all plausible calls with the same behavior (e.g. arr with optional n=len(arr)). Do count genuinely different parameter meanings that alter outputs.
When semantic evidence permits a reasoned choice, give the requested finite best-estimate point count and confidence even if reviewers disagree; do not use unknown merely to avoid judgment.

Use null only when the route from admissible questions and available simulator knowledge to required test behavior is not established, or the relevant oracle is unavailable. Null means not identifiable from evidence, not mathematically impossible or infinite.
Do not invent a rule from a few inconsistent assertions and label it the intended hidden requirement. A finite test-fitting implementation does not establish a legitimate Q3 clarification route.

recommended_two_axis_schema.minimum_q3_estimate: integer>=0 or null; best estimate for obtaining enough source-supported information to implement the current target
recommended_two_axis_schema.intended_contract_estimate: integer>=0 where a clear conventional intended contract exists, even if tests are inconsistent
recommended_two_axis_schema.questions: ordered one-fact questions, expected answers, per-question source support and inference consequences
recommended_two_axis_schema.remaining_after_sequence: test-distinguishing unresolved facts; must be empty before claiming a finite sufficient sequence

status_definitions.zero_inferred: No external fact needed under the stated high-end defaults; does not assert any generated implementation will pass.
status_definitions.finite_clarification_sequence: A finite sequence of estimated admissible Q3 questions resolves the identified independent behavioral choices after inference closure.
status_definitions.oracle_mismatch: Conventional intended behavior and evaluator disagree; report intended-contract count separately from an unestablished current-test clarification route.
status_definitions.source_cannot_identify: A needed behavior may exist, but effective user evidence cannot distinguish it without inventing facts or leaking implementation/tests.

disagreements.basis: For a list, two distinct elements conventionally means distinct occurrences/positions. Equal-valued zero occurrences may be paired without external knowledge. Public and reference are identical; a new Q3 fact is not clearly available.

Self-pair absolute difference is necessarily zero and i<j excludes it. Positive diagonal contribution is impossible under the named expression. All three actual assertions equal standard unordered sums: 74,10,188.

The coherent target highest power of two<=n is explicit. The simultaneous >n clause makes the contract unsatisfiable and is plausibly discarded by a strong reasoner; asking bound direction may fail SEARCH SPACE under that default.
Public prompt explicitly states subtractive notation, exposes IV for4, and calls additive clause contradictory. Asking whether to use subtractive notation recovers no undisclosed fact.

disagreements.recommendation: Do not count a second question to correct median arithmetic after resolving output representation.
disagreements.basis: Sorted [-10,4,6,10,20,1000] has median8. Public/ref15 is an arithmetic error, not an independent hidden requirement.

disagreements.recommendation: Roman-symbol order is inferred once actual Roman-numeral string output is established.
disagreements.basis: A sorted multiset of Roman letters is not ordinarily a Roman numeral encoding; do not count order independently solely due injected instruction.

disagreements.recommendation: Digest order is inferred once output is identified as MD5 hexadecimal digest.
disagreements.basis: Sorting digest characters destroys the named digest value; no extra order fact needed.

disagreements.recommendation: intended-contract estimate0; current-test route may remain null/oracle_mismatch.
disagreements.basis: Half-away-from-zero is explicit. Reproducing float-conversion precision loss is implementation/oracle behavior, not a legitimate hidden fact recoverable from the same reference.

disagreements.recommendation: Do not make finite current-test Q3 count by inventing uppercase-existence or first-character exclusion rule.
disagreements.basis: PYthon and BigData each contain two uppercase letters yet fallback expects1; reference only one anomalous assertion supports many rules.

disagreements.recommendation: Treat inferred slice assembly as an unvalidated explanatory hypothesis; do not ask for algorithm structure as a Q3 behavioral fact.
disagreements.basis: Rotation preserves length; fallback outputs length11 and7. Third-parameter meaning is plausible but not uniquely identified by public or reference prose.
